subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find dy and Δy for y = 5x² + 6x + 6 when x = 2 and Δx = 0.001.

mark_split.label: Find Δy from the exact change

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say how you get dy, and say what makes Δy a different number.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find dy from the derivative
steps.margin_note: First mark. Differentiate first, then multiply by Δx. Writing dy = (dy/dx)·Δx before any number goes in keeps this mark even if the arithmetic slips later.

recall.must_convey: That dy = (dy/dx)·Δx, with the derivative 10x + 6 found first and then multiplied by Δx.
accept: differentiate to get ten x plus six and multiply by delta x
d y equals d y by d x times delta x
the derivative at two is twenty six so d y is zero point zero two six
derivative teesi delta x tho multiply cheyyali
find d y by d x first then put x equals two

steps.why: dy is not the change in y. It is the derivative multiplied by Δx — the straight-line estimate of that change — so the mark is for differentiating and then multiplying, in that order.
common_mistakes: Writing dy = 10x + 6 and leaving out the ·Δx.
steps.memory_tip: dy uses the derivative once. Δy uses the function twice. d for derivative, Δ for difference.

steps.label: Find Δy from the exact change
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Keep every decimal place of (2.001)² = 4.004001. Δx is only 0.001 here, so dy and Δy differ in the sixth decimal place — rounding early erases the difference the question is about.

recall.must_convey: That Δy = f(x + Δx) − f(x) = f(2.001) − f(2) = 0.026005, the exact change.
accept: delta y is f of two point zero zero one minus f of two
the exact change is zero point zero two six zero zero five
rendu values lo substitute chesi subtract cheyyali
delta y is the real change and d y is only the estimate
heard_as: f of two point zero zero one
zero two six zero zero five

steps.why: Δy is the real change in y, so the function has to be worked out at both points. With Δx this small the two answers agree to five decimal places, which shows how good the straight-line estimate becomes as Δx shrinks.
common_mistakes: Rounding (2.001)² to 4.004 and losing the 0.000005 difference.
Stopping at dy when the question asks for both numbers.
steps.memory_tip: Δy is the after value minus the before value, in that order — a negative Δy is allowed and simply means y went down.

insider_note: dy uses the derivative and is approximate; Δy is the EXACT difference f(x + Δx) − f(x). Both are asked, so both must be computed, and they differ only in the sixth decimal place.
